title: Ethiopian Spiced Lemon
community: Ethiopian lakeside restaurants — the lemon-kibbeh condiment
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Lemon-Kibbeh Condiment — lemon juice mixed with melted kibbeh and a pinch of salt, served warm alongside grilled fish. The simplest of the Ethiopian condiments — the acid of lemon cutting through the fat of kibbeh into a bright, clean sauce.
longDesc: This simple condiment is a lakeside restaurant staple — served warm in a small pot alongside grilled fish, the lemon-kibbeh provides an acid-fat balance that perfectly complements the charcoal-grilled berbere fish.
steps: Add lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Stir briefly — it will not fully emulsify.
Serve warm in a small ramekin.
Guests dip their fish or drizzle over.
chefTips: Serve immediately — the temporary emulsion breaks quickly.
Warm kibbeh plus cold lemon juice creates the brief emulsion.
commonMistakes: Cold kibbeh — doesn't combine with lemon.
cookingScience: See ETH150 for lemon-kibbeh emulsion science.
culturalNote: Lemon-kibbeh condiment is the lakeside restaurant's simplest and most useful sauce — drizzled over grilled tilapia at a table overlooking Lake Tana, it is one of Ethiopia's most satisfying simple pleasures.
